_note: Running costs, read by sim/. Staff pay comes from staff.json (hours x hourly_pay x (1 + on_cost_rate)). Card fees and carrier costs are charged by the engine itself on every order and parcel (they match tools/world/money.mjs: 1.5% + 20p, and £2.90 standard, £5.10 next-day, £6.80 chilled), so the simulator reads them from the ledger and does not charge them twice. The engine's own fixed-cost lines (wages, rent, software, marketing_spend) are ignored by the simulator, which charges the ones below instead. Numbers per month are for a team sized for staff.json's reference_orders_per_day; the simulator scales them with --scale.
assumptions: Staff are paid for their contracted hours whether busy or not; extra work is overtime at 1.5 times for people marked overtime: true.
Time saved by a tool is valued at the pay of the people whose task minutes fell (pay including on-costs), because that is what it would cost to buy back.
Rent, software, insurance and utilities do not change with a tool, so they cancel out in the comparison; they are there so each run's profit is real.
Packaging is charged per order and is not in the engine's cost of goods.
